summary: MFA device relink breaks service-token refresh for analytics console sessions
description:
Issue summary:
Some users and service accounts are unable to refresh short-lived service tokens after an Okta MFA device relink. Affected sessions show a 401/invalid_grant from the token broker when attempting to renew console session tokens.

Impact:
Several internal engineering and on-call users report they cannot refresh active sessions in the analytics console; automated runbook runners that call the console API intermittently fail token refresh and enter a degraded retry loop. Business impact: delayed incident triage and dashboards failing to update for affected teams.

Environment:
- Prod (us-east region)
- Okta identity provider (org: redwood-prod)
- Auth-proxy version: v2.14.1

Steps to reproduce:
1) Create or identify service account with device-bound MFA (device attestation enabled).
2) Relink MFA device for the user/service in Okta (remove old device, enroll new).
3) With an existing long-lived console session, trigger a token refresh (wait for token expiry or call refresh endpoint).
4) Observe token broker returning 400/invalid_grant and console forcing re-login.

Observed logs (auth-proxy / token-broker):
- "token-broker: refresh failed: invalid_grant - device_binding_mismatch"
- "okta-scim: profile update: deviceRelink=true for user: svc-analytics-01"

Additional context:
This appears correlated to Okta's device relink flow when the device attestation claim (device_id/device_fingerprint) changes but the service-token refresh path still expects the prior assertion. The console's refresh flow does not gracefully fallback to interactive re-auth and instead returns transient 401s for downstream service accounts, causing retry storms from runbook-runner processes.
steps_to_reproduce: Relink MFA device in Okta for a user with existing session
Trigger token refresh on analytics-console session
Observe invalid_grant errors in token-broker logs
comments: Support (2026-03-10) - jasmine.patel: Customer impact reported by internal SRE pager rotation. Initial triage: token-broker returns invalid_grant after device relink.
SRE (2026-03-10) - rafael.gomez: Reproduced in staging by simulating device re-enroll. Token refresh fails for sessions created prior to relink. Adding auth-proxy and okta-scim teams to investigate.

Auth-proxy (2026-03-11) - megan.lee: We see refresh path validates device_attestation_claim against stored session metadata. If it mismatches, we currently reject rather than triggering session invalidation. Proposed fix: treat mismatch as interactive-required and emit clear audit_event.

Okta-Platform (2026-03-11) - daniel.kim: Okta returns new device fingerprint after relink; we can add mapping for previous device_id in SCIM patch but that is an org-level change. Raising with identity infra to discuss safe migration.

SRE (2026-03-12) - rafael.gomez: Implemented temporary mitigation: token-broker will return 403/interactive_required with a clear message for mismatched device attestations to stop automated refresh retries. Rolling patch to prod-us-east (canary=10%).
investigation_notes:
Hypothesis A: token-broker is too strict and treats any device attribute mismatch as invalid_grant instead of interactive-required.
Evidence: Logs show 'device_binding_mismatch' error code instead of 'interactive_required'.

Hypothesis B: SCIM sync after device relink is delayed causing transient mismatch between Okta and session store.
Evidence: SCIM webhook delivery timestamps show 15-30s delay in some cases.

Relevant links: Slack #support-sre thread (https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C0123456) and Grafana dashboard for token-broker error rates (https://grafana.redwood.com/d/token-broker/token-refresh-errors)
resolution: Mitigation rolled to prod-us-east: token-broker now maps device-attestation mismatches to 403 interactive_required with a machine-readable reason. This prevents automated runbook-runners from entering tight retry loops. Permanent fix: auth-proxy PR to update refresh flow and add audit trail merged in PR 4321; plan to deploy globally after QA (ETA 2026-03-18). Follow-ups: update runbook 'auth/token-refresh' to include guidance, and schedule Okta SCIM cadence review with identity team.
next_steps: Complete global rollout of auth-proxy change (deploy to eu-west and apac)
Update internal runbook with new error handling and remediation steps
Coordinate with identity team to reduce SCIM webhook delays and consider preserving previous device_id aliases for a short window
sla_notes: First response: 2026-03-10 09:22 UTC. Owner: SRE. Target mitigation applied within 48 hours. Customer-facing impact limited to internal teams; no external customers affected.
